props.name: zinc oxide-chromia catalyst (19 wt.% chromia)
activation energy
props.statement: The plot of log k vs. 1/T is a straight line whose slope gives an apparent activation energy of 26.1 kcal/mol.

props.name: alpha 0.3 fits
props.statement: The integrated rate equation is well satisfied with α = 0.3: the plots for different pressures at a given temperature fall on one straight line through the origin; with α = 0.1 they diverge with rising temperature and with α = 0.7 with lowering temperature.

props.name: byproducts small
props.statement: The product contained water, methyl formate and formaldehyde as by-products and a little increase in carbon dioxide was found in the exit gas; the quantities of by-products are very small, so the methanol concentration calculated from the gas consumed is correct.

props.name: calculated concentration agrees with collected
props.statement: The methanol concentration determined from the quantity of methanol actually obtained agreed well with that calculated from the gas consumed.

props.name: concentration vs ratio
props.statement: At high H2/CO ratios the methanol concentration remains small; it increases rapidly at first with decreasing ratio and then slowly below a ratio of four; this tendency is less marked at higher space velocities, where the concentration remains far below equilibrium.

props.name: conversion efficiency pressure
props.statement: The conversion efficiency changes with total pressure more remarkably at the lower temperature and less so at the higher temperature; at 350 °C it becomes nearly constant, independent of the total pressure.

props.name: efficiency vs ratio
props.statement: At high H2/CO ratios the conversion efficiency is high and tends to decrease monotonously as the ratio lowers to two.

props.name: equilibrium between newitt and ewell
props.statement: The equilibrium constants obtained here are intermediate between Newitt's and Ewell's values, and the line through them runs parallel to Ewell's.

props.name: initial rate not determinable
props.statement: Accurate determination of the initial rate was difficult in the present work, since the results do not contain enough methanol concentrations at very high space velocities.

props.name: k independent of pressure ratio sv
props.statement: The rate constant is independent of the total pressure (α = 0.3, Fig. 9) and hardly changes with the H2/CO ratio (Fig. 10); z calculated with a value of k agrees well with the experimental data over a wide range of space velocity (Fig. 11).

props.name: no methane olefine
props.statement: Hardly any methane or olefine was detected in the gas after the synthesis.

props.name: rate equation represents results
props.statement: The derived rate equation r = kd{(pCO·p²H2)^0.7 − pCH3OH·(pCO·p²H2)^−0.3/K} represents the experimental results satisfactorily over relatively wide ranges of pressure, H2/CO ratio and space velocity.

props.name: reactant adsorption rds worse
props.statement: The premise that the adsorption of a reactant is rate-determining leads to a rate equation representing the results less satisfactorily.

props.name: methanol desorption rate-determining on a logarithmic isotherm
props.statement: The rate of methanol synthesis is governed by the desorption of methanol as the rate-determining step, with a logarithmic adsorption isotherm; neither the adsorption of hydrogen nor that of carbon monoxide is rate-determining.

props.name: Natta's rate equation could also fit these results
props.statement: By choice of suitable values for the constants, the rate equation of Natta et al. should represent the present experimental results well, though the choice requires tedious trial-and-error calculation.

props.name: space-time yield nearly independent of H2/CO 2-4 in industrial synthesis
props.statement: For H2/CO ratios limited to 2-4, in industrial synthesis where the space velocity is relatively high and the methanol concentration remains considerably below equilibrium, the space-time yield will remain nearly the same, independent of the ratio.

props.name: reaction between adsorbed H2 and CO as rate-determining step (alternative)
props.statement: Other steps, such as the reaction between the adsorbed hydrogen and the adsorbed carbon monoxide, might also be adopted as the rate-determining step; not pursued because the data could be explained by the methanol-desorption concept.
